- **Stage:** Lint
  - **Runs:** `cargo fmt --check`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features fake-agent -- -D warnings`; `cargo check` with one `-p` per crate listed in `scripts/sync-crates.txt` (no `--features`, so no tokio; target set `viola-core`, `viola-pty`, `viola-state`, `viola-agent-claude`, four since `viola-channel` left the list at chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers — its Tokio client sits behind its `tokio` feature and its normal graph is held by the tree form `scripts/channel-tokio-free.sh`, Supply-chain row — each joining the list with its crate; an empty list fails; job `lint`); `bash scripts/orphans-check.sh --probe && bash scripts/orphans-check.sh` (cargo-modules 0.27.0: `cargo modules orphans -p <pkg> {--lib | --bin <name>} [--features <required features>] --deny` for every lib/bin target from `cargo metadata --no-deps`, last line `orphans-check: N/N targets clean`; the probe fires on each of its two planted orphans, last line `orphans-check probes: 2/2 fired, control clean`). `cargo modules dependencies --acyclic` is an on-demand boundary review, not a gate: at cargo-modules 0.27.0 every type and its own inherent method read as a cycle whatever the filters (measured at chunk 2026-09-24-workspace-tree-and-code-graph-planes, 3 of 4 targets). The rmcp release-graph assertion is the lint step `rmcp features (exactly server + transport-io, non-vacuous)` (every OS, after `Lint probes`; chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers): `bash scripts/rmcp-features.sh` runs `cargo tree -e features -p viola --edges normal --target all -i rmcp --no-dedupe --prefix depth`, rmcp must be present and the features a non-rmcp package requests exactly `server transport-io`, last line `rmcp-features: server transport-io`.
 Beside CI, a chunk plan may list a check-only Windows-target clippy as a chunk gate entry on the Linux dev host, which does not build the `cfg(windows)` code CI lints (first listed by chunk 2026-10-13-epoch-4-cleanup; `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/wincheck cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features fake-agent --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc -- -D warnings`, nothing linked, the target std installed as host preparation): neither a CI step nor a `pre-push` stage.
 Beside it, a check-only macOS-target clippy is a recipe on the Linux dev host (`CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/maccheck cargo clippy … --target aarch64-apple-darwin`, nothing linked, the target std installed as host preparation by `rustup target add aarch64-apple-darwin`); it reproduced CI's `lint (macos-latest)` error line for line, as measured at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-26-server-verification-before-any-frame/evidence/operator-pass.md`: neither a CI step, nor a `pre-push` stage, nor a plan gate entry.
  - **Parallel:** per OS matrix
  - **Cache:** Swatinem/rust-cache v2.9.2 (SHA-pinned; key: OS + toolchain + `Cargo.lock`), in `ci.yml` only

- **Stage:** Supply-chain
  - **Runs:** ubuntu job `supply-chain`, fail-closed `shell: bash` steps: `cargo deny --format json check` (`deny.toml`: advisories, licences, sources, bans, the bans holding a `[[bans.features]]` table that denies serde_json's `unbounded_depth`); `cargo deny --manifest-path fuzz/Cargo.toml --format json check advisories sources` into `target/supply-chain/deny-fuzz.json`, run from the repo root (under `fuzz/`, rustup would demand the fuzz nightly); the tokio ban once per crate in `scripts/sync-crates.txt` as sole root, `cargo deny --config deny-sync.toml --manifest-path crates/<crate>/Cargo.toml check bans`, then, in the same step `Tokio ban per sync crate (sole root)`, `bash scripts/channel-tokio-free.sh` (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers: `cargo tree -p viola-channel -e normal --target all -i tokio --prefix none` must print no `tokio v` line — exit 0 "nothing to print", or exit 101 "did not match" while tokio is not in the lock; presence read from the printed line, never the exit — and its control with `--features tokio` must print one; verdict `channel-tokio-free: ok`); `bash scripts/deny-probes.sh` (a permanent negative probe per ban + a clean control, last line `deny-probes: 14/14 banned, control clean`: the thirteen bans one probe each (the serde_json `unbounded_depth` ban's row `serde_json-unbounded-depth` firing `error[feature-banned]`), plus probe `channel-tokio-edge` — a throwaway workspace with a normal tokio edge must fail the tree form — with its channel control, the same edge behind a `tokio` feature passing); `zizmor --format=json .github/workflows/`. The deny (root and fuzz) and zizmor JSON go to `target/supply-chain/`, uploaded `if: always()` as artifact `supply-chain` (7 days; admissible by content, obs-plan §8 item 6). Weekly: `nightly.yml` job `advisories` runs `cargo deny check advisories` and `cargo deny --manifest-path fuzz/Cargo.toml check advisories`, on `schedule` + `workflow_dispatch`
  - **Parallel:** single job (+ the weekly job)
  - **Cache:** rust-cache (`ci.yml` job only; `nightly.yml` none)

  - **Runs:** `agent-run run --coverage` (cargo-llvm-cov 0.9.1 under nextest). In CI this is the per-OS test job; on `windows-2025` its `ConPTY vendor verification` step runs first (`bash scripts/conpty-vendor.sh --verify`: the committed `vendor/conpty/1.24.260710001/x64/` bytes equal the pinned nupkg and carry the Microsoft signer, last line `conpty-vendor: verified <version>`; then `--probe`: four refusals and a control, last line `conpty-vendor probe: 4/4 refused, control clean`), and the coverage run covers the `conpty_sideload` integration binary (`[[test]]`, required-features `fake-agent`) with the rest. Its one instrumented nextest run replaces the Unit, Integration and `run --e2e` rows, which are the local `agent-run` equivalents, and the doctest run follows it. Each job's last step is `viola-harness gate --require <suites>`: the per-OS test job uses `coverage,doctest`, and the Perf, Fuzz replay and MSRV jobs use `perf`, `fuzz-replay` and `nextest-unit`

  - **Cache:** rust-cache

  - **Runs:** ci.yml job `release` (`fail-fast: false`): `bash scripts/release-check.sh --probe` (last line `release-check probes: 5/5 refused, control clean`), then `bash scripts/release-check.sh`, which runs `cargo build --release --locked --bin viola --message-format=json` (fake agent excluded: feature off) and judges that build's own `compiler-artifact` records. It prints `release-check: viola only` or fails on an artifact built with a test-only feature (`test-support`, `fake-agent`), on a test-only binary or on no executable, and never lists `target/release/`.   - **Runs:** `viola-harness gate`, which reads `junit-*.xml`, `run-summary.json`, the llvm-cov JSON summary and the hyperfine JSON, and exits non-zero on any §10 breach

Every workflow (`ci.yml`, `nightly.yml`, `windows-mutants.yml`) has `permissions: {}` at the top and `contents: read` per job. Every `uses:` is SHA-pinned; zizmor `unpinned-uses` is the assertion. Tools are installed with taiki-e/install-action v2.87.19 (SHA-pinned) as `tool: cargo-nextest@0.9.146,cargo-llvm-cov@0.9.1,cargo-mutants@27.1.0,cargo-deny@0.20.2`; `windows-mutants.yml` installs `tool: cargo-nextest@0.9.146,cargo-mutants@27.1.0` with the same action, and `tests/contract_windows_mutation_scope.rs` asserts those two pins equal the `test` job's `tool:` line. hyperfine 1.20.0, cargo-modules 0.27.0 and zizmor 1.30.1 are installed with `cargo install --locked <crate>@<version>` in the jobs that invoke them. G2 (`scripts/g2-zero-panics.sh`, in the `test` and `perf` jobs), `scripts/orphans-check.sh` (`lint`) and `scripts/release-check.sh` (`release`) use the runner-provided `jq`, never installed: the `test` and `perf` jobs presence-check it (`jq --version`) and all three scripts refuse with `tool-missing: jq`. ripgrep 15.2.0, the G1/G3 tool, comes from `scripts/install-ripgrep.sh` (pinned, checksum-verified official release) in the `lint` job. cargo-fuzz 0.13.2 is installed with `cargo install --locked`, only in the `fuzz-replay` and nightly `fuzz` jobs, with the channel from `fuzz/rust-toolchain.toml`. See §3 Bootstrap `ci-tool-install`. rustfmt and clippy come from `rust-toolchain.toml` `components`, installed by the `rustup toolchain install` step (no toolchain action; the MSRV and fuzz jobs, which need a different toolchain, name theirs). cargo-deny and zizmor run as the pinned CLIs above; cargo-deny-action and zizmor-action are not used, so each tool has exactly one version source.
 The local pre-push gate runs natively on the Linux dev host and installs nothing: its `tools` stage checks the host's `cc`, the `rust-toolchain.toml` channel, the pins it parses from the `test` job's `tool:` line (cargo-nextest 0.9.146, cargo-mutants 27.1.0, cargo-llvm-cov 0.9.1, as read on the Linux dev host 2026-10-04), refusing a missing or off-pin tool with `tool-missing` / `tool-pin-mismatch` — so ci.yml stays the one version source. No provisioning script remains. cargo-deny 0.20 takes `--config <path>` as a global option before the subcommand; `check -c` is rejected (as measured on cargo-deny 0.20.2, dev host, 2026-09-24).
No workflow (`ci.yml`, `nightly.yml`, `windows-mutants.yml`) has a `concurrency:` block: a concurrency group cancels pending runs even with `cancel-in-progress: false`, which would drop a push's `always()` gate and upload chain. zizmor's pedantic `concurrency-limits` finding is declined and stays visible (3 low, one per workflow; zizmor 1.30.1 on the dev host, 2026-10-04).
